about: Calques and false friends commonly found in English written by speakers of Polish, each with the form to use instead. The list is based on errors that speakers of Polish are generally known to make, and is not yet confirmed by errors found in real use. "find" is a case-insensitive regular expression. It must match "example", which contains the error, and must not match "correct".

calques.why: Polish "aktualny" means "current". In English, "actual" means "real", as opposed to "supposed".
calques.example: Install the actual version of the plugin.
calques.correct: Install the current version of the plugin.

calques.why: Polish "aktualnie" means "currently". In English, "actually" means "in fact".
calques.example: Only two formats are actually supported.
calques.correct: Only two formats are currently supported.

calques.why: Polish "ewentualnie" means "possibly" or "if necessary". In English, "eventually" means "in the end".
calques.example: Eventually we can add a second reader.
calques.correct: If necessary, we can add a second reader.

calques.why: Polish "kontrola" means "a check" or "an inspection". In English, "control" means "manage" or "restrain".
calques.example: The script controls whether the file exists.
calques.correct: The script checks whether the file exists.

calques.why: Polish "konkretny" means "specific". In English, "concrete" means "tangible", as opposed to "abstract".
calques.example: In this concrete case the hook stops the push.
calques.correct: In this particular case the hook stops the push.

calques.why: Polish "zależeć od", translated word for word, gives "depend from". In English, "depend" is followed by "on".
calques.example: The result depends from the configuration.
calques.correct: The result depends on the configuration.

calques.use: "for" before a length of time, "since" before a point in time
calques.why: Polish "od" is followed by a length of time. In English, only a point in time follows "since", and a length of time follows "for".
calques.example: The test has failed since three days.
calques.correct: The test has failed for three days.

calques.why: Polish "realizować" means "carry out". In English, "realize" means "become aware of", and only rarely "achieve".
calques.example: We realized the migration in two steps.
calques.correct: We carried out the migration in two steps.

calques.use: take a photo, take a screenshot
calques.why: In English, you take a photo or a screenshot. "Make" is copied from the verb used in the writer's own language.
calques.example: Make a screenshot of the error.
calques.correct: Take a screenshot of the error.

calques.use: information, advice, software, feedback, equipment, knowledge, hardware (no plural)
calques.why: In English these nouns are uncountable and have no plural. The plural is copied from the writer's own language, where the corresponding nouns are countable.
calques.example: The log keeps all informations about the run.
calques.correct: The log keeps all the information about the run.

calques.use: what it looks like, or how it looks
calques.why: English uses either "what … looks like" or "how … looks". "How … looks like" mixes the two, following the pattern of the writer's own language.
calques.example: The page shows how the report looks like.
calques.correct: The page shows what the report looks like.
